name: SQL injection
mental_model: Untrusted data changes the structure or meaning of a database command instead of remaining a bound value.
security_property: User-controlled values must not alter database command structure, authorization, or selected result boundaries.
root_causes: Database permissions broader than the application requires
signals: Input changes query shape or row count
Database errors correlate with controlled structure changes
A query builder concatenates untrusted values

hypothesis_templates.statement: When {actor} controls {input}, {query_boundary} may treat the value as query structure and expose {controlled_result} beyond the intended lookup.
preconditions: Only a local synthetic dataset is used
The experiment has a strict row and effect budget
hypothesis_templates.expected_safe_behaviour: The value is bound as data and the intended result set is preserved.
hypothesis_templates.expected_vulnerable_behaviour: The value changes query structure or the controlled result set.
hypothesis_templates.falsifier: Parameter binding preserves structure and every controlled variation returns only the intended rows.
stop_conditions: The database boundary is not explicitly authorised

safe_test_pattern: Use a read-only in-memory dataset, a neutral structural marker, strict result-count limits, and a parameterized negative control.
positive_controls: A valid named lookup returns exactly its synthetic row
negative_controls: The same untrusted value is bound as data and cannot change the result set
falsifiers: The structure is fixed and values are parameterized
Observed variation is ordinary application validation rather than database interpretation

minimum_evidence.description: Exact synthetic query inputs and bounded result-set difference.
The intended query and row-access boundary for the controlled actor.
Parameterized negative control and intended-query positive control.
Fresh in-memory database repeat with identical synthetic rows.
Human statement limited to the demonstrated synthetic row boundary.

common_false_positives: Result differences caused by application filtering
Database errors without controlled query influence
impact_boundaries: An error does not prove injection
Read influence does not prove write, file, command, or administrative capability
minimum_impact_rules: Do not enumerate beyond the single controlled contrast
Never attempt destructive or out-of-band behaviour
remediation: Constrain database privileges and error exposure
programme_policy_considerations: Confirm injection testing and automation limits
Avoid time, load, or out-of-band techniques unless explicitly permitted
Stop at the smallest controlled result difference

revisions.summary: Initial query-structure card and read-only synthetic fixture.
